## Open — known gaps in what ships today

- **V12** headless Chromium on a software GL stack, not Safari: a drag never scrolling or zooming the page in iPhone Safari, the safe-area insets under a notch and the audio start after the first touch need a look on a real iPhone. No haptics in a browser. Browser speed is not iPhone speed: no performance claim. The game's own save writes (`progress.txt`) reach IndexedDB by the same flush; only a file written in the page was reloaded.
- **V11** desktop captures and tests only; the feel of the slow motion, the haptic and the tune on a phone is the owner's TestFlight check. No device measurement: the confetti is under 200 small shapes (not a performance task).
- **V10** none known; desktop captures only, no device measurement (not a performance change).
- **V9** the captures are desktop SDL at 1x. Phone 3x appearance and the 200 ms pop's tactile feel remain the owner's TestFlight check. This task has no device performance goal. An installation with a saved legacy palette kept it until V10, which removed the other palettes.
- **V8** sprites have no mipmaps, so art shrunk past about 2x aliases; the 40-point flower in the 1x desktop capture shows it. Text has no kerning. The capture is desktop 1x; the 3x phone draws from the larger bakes, not yet seen on a device. No game art, look or gameplay changes.
- **V7** Yotam chooses a theme. Accepting the revised plan starts Garden Pop's implementation; another theme needs a named change first. The 180-220 ms hit settle is a proposed target, not a measured animation. Damage cues during motion, BMP alpha support and iPhone performance need a playable check after acceptance. Runtime tests, player-path and device checks are not applicable to this concept round. No game, engine or palette changes.
- **V5** the bot is not a person; whether relief feels too easy (the bot wins 100%) and whether level 10's losses feel near (level 10's losses rarely see the goal, 5%) are Yotam's calls on TestFlight. Speed and Ping break nothing, so the numbers cannot show levels 5 and 7 teach them. Device performance is not applicable.
- **V4** the player path on a phone or simulator (play level 1 to a win, see level 2, lose, retry) is Yotam's TestFlight check; the Windows tests drive the same Game handlers. Seeds and numbers are T11's. Debug settings other than the level are still session-only (T9). Device performance is not applicable.
- **V3** Yotam's phone review of the numbers and of tapping the denser panel. A bomb near the wall can still exist when the bomb size is raised after the grid was generated. Device performance is not applicable.
- **V2** Yotam's phone review. At 60 by 100 a cell is about 6.5 points at minimum zoom, so play needs zooming in. Device performance is not applicable.

## Every version

### Active — what ships today

- **V12** TapDemo runs in a phone browser (D11)
- **V11** Breaking the goal plays a festive, Peggle-style celebration (D10)
- **V10** TapDemo has one look: Garden Pop (D9)
- **V9** Garden Pop plays with material damage and a local hit pop (D8)
- **V8** Transparent, cropped sprites and baked real-font text (D7)
- **V7** Themed reskin concepts with material damage and hit-effect studies (G12)
- **V5** Level seeds tuned by simulated play to their experiences (D6)
- **V4** Ten fixed levels, retries on the same field (D5)
- **V3** Power-up tuning and snapped straight shots (D4)
- **V2** Debug grid size, glow rate and power-up weights (D3)

### Superseded — replaced, kept for the record

- **V6** Three screen reskin concepts for owner selection (G12) → V7 — the owner requested stronger themes and visible material damage
- **V1** Four colour schemes with distinct fog and cavities (D2) → V10 — only Garden Pop remains
